correctness.rationale: For sufficiently small radii, a ball centered in component i sees only p_i times the i-th measure, giving the exact identity C_mu equals the sum of p_i squared times C_i. Invariance keeps single orbits in their starting component; cross-component two-orbit counts eventually vanish. Substitution of the assumed local laws yields the stated a_i over A limits. A putative limit one on every positive-weight component would force the sum of squared weights to equal one, impossible for a nontrivial mixture.

evidence: The prior theorems concern broad mixing/equidistribution behavior rather than the exact finite-mixture denominator once local laws are assumed.

final_claim: For a finite positively separated invariant mixture with componentwise pair-correlation laws and comparable local correlation-integral scales, global normalization gives exact component limits a_i divided by the squared-weight scale A and zero for cross-component two-orbit pairs, so a nontrivial mixture cannot have global limit one almost everywhere.
limitations: Requires finitely many positively separated invariant supports and assumed local pair-correlation laws.
